locator.text: Display 67.4, p. 67, in the proof of Lemma 6.2

provenance.note: machine audit: worker, gate, reviewer; not confirmed by a human

verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. Every piece of the display is stated, but as three declarations rather than one. (a) The set equality: `preimage_nativeRectangle_sheets` gives (torusCovering^[g.gap])⁻¹' nativeRectangle g r = ⋃_{i : Sheet g.gap} sheetRectangle g r i; unfolding sheetRectangle/liftedRectangle/Geometry.point turns the i = [k] member into quotientPoint ((coverPower g.gap).symm (g.center + latticePoint k + g.basis z)), which is the paper's J_g^{-Δ}(c_γ + k + ξ v_r + η v_t) (mod Z²) once g.basis = slotChart v_r v_t (slotChart_apply z = z.1 • v_r + z.2 • v_t, TorusAverages.lean:488). The index type Sheet g.gap = Frequency ⧸ (coverHom g.gap).range is literally Z²/J_g^Δ Z². The parameter domain is Metric.ball (0 : Plane) r₀, and the product norm on Plane is the max norm, so the ball is exactly {|ξ|,|η| < r₀} (stated in the docstring at TorusAverages.lean:169-170). Lean leaves g.basis an arbitrary Plane ≃L[ℝ] Plane, so it is more general than the paper's fixed radial/temporal pair. (b) The paper writes ⊔ (disjoint union); Lean's equality uses ⋃ and disjointness is the separate `pairwise_disjoint_sheetRectangles_of_injOn`, conditional on InjOn quotientPoint over the chart — the hypothesis the paper leaves implicit in its choice of small r₀ (`pairwise_disjoint_sheetRectangles`, line 247, discharges it from ‖g.basis‖ * r < 1/2). (c) The count: `card_sheet` states #(Z²/J_g^Δ Z²) = 14^Δ. The paper's middle expression |det J_g|^Δ is not stated anywhere I found: Lean reaches 14 through the surjective residue homomorphism Frequency →+ ZMod 14 (TorusCoverLattice.lean:28-63), never through a determinant of J_g, so the identity |det J_g| = 14 for [[3,1],[1,5]] is not a Lean statement. That is a route difference in an arithmetic identity whose value, 14, Lean does state.
